title: When, until, so that: cuando llegues, para que sepas
summary: Talk about the future with cuando, en cuanto, hasta que and antes de que + subjunctive, and say why with para or para que.
focus: The subjunctive in future time clauses and purpose clauses, and the infinitive when the subject is the same
content:
## Cuando + subjunctive: the future that hasn't happened yet

When the moment after **cuando** is still to come, Spanish puts it in the **present subjunctive**. Habits and past events are facts, so they keep the **indicative**.

| situation | example |
|---|---|
| future (not yet) | **Cuando llegues, te llamo.** When you arrive, I'll call you. |
| habit | **Cuando llego a casa, me ducho.** When I get home, I have a shower. |
| past | **Cuando llegué, cenamos.** When I arrived, we had dinner. |

Never put the future after **cuando**. Say **cuando llegues**, not ~~cuando llegarás~~. The question word **¿cuándo?** is different: **¿Cuándo llegas?** takes the indicative.

## En cuanto, hasta que, después de que… and antes de que

**En cuanto** (as soon as), **hasta que** (until) and **después de que** (after) follow the same rule as **cuando**:

- **En cuanto sepa algo, te aviso.** As soon as I know something, I'll let you know.
- **Te espero hasta que salgas.** I'll wait for you until you come out.
- **Después de que se vayan, limpiamos.** After they leave, we'll clean up.
- **Siempre leo hasta que me duermo.** I always read until I fall asleep. (habit: indicative)

**Antes de que** (before) is the exception: it **always** takes the subjunctive, even for habits: **Siempre salgo antes de que se despierten los niños.** (Its past form is coming at B2.)

## Same subject? Use the infinitive

When both halves have the same subject, drop **que** and use **antes de**, **después de** or **hasta** + infinitive:

- **Ceno antes de salir.** I have dinner before I go out. (I eat, I go out)
- **Ceno antes de que salgas.** I have dinner before you go out. (two people)
- **Después de comer, damos un paseo.** After eating, we go for a walk.
- **No paro hasta terminar.** I won't stop until I finish.

The infinitive is shorter and more natural, so use it whenever the subject is the same.

## Para + infinitive or para que + subjunctive

Purpose works the same way. The same person takes **para** + infinitive, and a different person takes **para que** + subjunctive:

- **Ahorro para comprar un coche.** I'm saving (in order) to buy a car.
- **Ahorro para que mis hijos puedan estudiar.** I'm saving so that my children can study.
- **Te lo explico para que lo entiendas.** I'm explaining it to you so that you understand it.

**Para que** always takes the subjunctive, because a purpose is never a fact yet. Say **para que entiendas**, not ~~para que entiendes~~.

vocabulary.example: Cuando llegues a casa, mándame un mensaje.
vocabulary.example_meaning: When you get home, send me a message.

vocabulary.example_meaning: Wait here until your brother comes back.

vocabulary.meaning: after (+ a clause with its own subject)
vocabulary.example: Después de que se vayan los invitados, limpiamos la cocina.
vocabulary.example_meaning: After the guests leave, we'll clean the kitchen.

vocabulary.example: Quiero hablar con ella antes de que se vaya.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I want to talk to her before she leaves.

vocabulary.example: Lávate las manos antes de comer.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Wash your hands before eating.

vocabulary.example: Después de cenar, vemos una película.
vocabulary.example_meaning: After dinner, we watch a film.

vocabulary.example: Te dejo las llaves para que puedas entrar.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'm leaving you the keys so that you can get in.

vocabulary.example: Avísame cuando termines.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Let me know when you finish.

vocabulary.example: Cuando nos mudemos, tendremos un jardín.
vocabulary.example_meaning: When we move, we'll have a garden.

vocabulary.example: Ahorro un poco cada mes para comprar una bici.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I save a little every month to buy a bike.

vocabulary.example: Cuando mi padre se jubile, quiere vivir en el pueblo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: When my father retires, he wants to live in the village.

vocabulary.example: Estudio todos los días para aprobar el examen.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I study every day to pass the exam.

quiz.explanation: The arrival is still to come, so cuando takes the present subjunctive: 'Cuando llegues a Madrid, te llamaré.' Cuando is never followed by the future.

quiz.prompt: Normalmente, cuando ___ a casa, me ducho.
quiz.explanation: Normalmente marks a habit, and habits are facts: cuando + indicative. 'Cuando llego a casa, me ducho.'

quiz.prompt: Ayer, cuando ___ a casa, vi a Pedro en la calle.
quiz.explanation: Ayer puts it in the past: a past event is a fact, so cuando takes the indicative (preterite): 'cuando llegué'.
hints: Watch the accent: llegué (preterite) vs llegue (subjunctive).

quiz.prompt: En cuanto ___ (aprobar, yo) el examen, te aviso.
quiz.explanation: En cuanto works like cuando: a future moment takes the present subjunctive. Aprobar keeps its stem change: apruebo becomes apruebe.
hints: From apruebo, change the final -o to -e.

quiz.prompt: Llámame antes de que ___ el tren.
quiz.explanation: Antes de que always takes the subjunctive: 'antes de que salga el tren'.
hints: Antes de que has no exceptions.

quiz.prompt: No nos vamos hasta que ___ (terminar, nosotros) el trabajo.
quiz.explanation: Finishing the work is still to come, so hasta que takes the subjunctive: terminar becomes terminemos.

quiz.prompt: Me lavo los dientes antes de ___.
quiz.explanation: Same subject (I brush my teeth, I go to bed): antes de + infinitive, with the pronoun attached: 'antes de acostarme'.
hints: Who goes to bed? The same person who brushes their teeth.
After a preposition Spanish uses the infinitive.

quiz.prompt: Ahorramos para que nuestros hijos ___ (poder) estudiar.
quiz.explanation: Different subjects (we save, our children study), so para que + subjunctive: poder becomes puedan (o changes to ue).
hints: Para que is always followed by the subjunctive.
poder is a boot verb: pueda, puedas, pueda…

quiz.prompt: Después de que mi madre se ___ (jubilar), nos mudaremos a la costa.
quiz.explanation: The retirement is still to come, so después de que takes the subjunctive: jubilar becomes (se) jubile.
hints: An -ar verb takes -e in the subjunctive.

conversations.title: Moving to Valencia
conversations.scenario: Javier is about to move to Valencia; his friend Clara, who moved to Bilbao a few years ago, helps him plan.

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: So, when are you moving to Valencia?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Cuando termine el contrato del piso, en junio más o menos.
lines.meaning: When the lease on the flat ends, in June more or less.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¿Y vas a buscar trabajo allí antes de irte?
lines.meaning: And are you going to look for work there before you leave?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Sí, quiero tener algo antes de que se acabe mi dinero.
lines.meaning: Yes, I want to have something before my money runs out.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Normal. Cuando yo me mudé a Bilbao, tardé tres meses en encontrar algo.
lines.meaning: Makes sense. When I moved to Bilbao, it took me three months to find something.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Por eso ahorro un poco cada mes, para no tener problemas.
lines.meaning: That's why I save a bit every month, so as not to have problems.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Muy bien. Oye, te dejo mi coche para que lleves tus cosas.
lines.meaning: Great. Listen, I'll lend you my car so that you can take your things.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¿En serio? ¡Gracias! Te lo devuelvo en cuanto llegue.
lines.meaning: Really? Thanks! I'll give it back as soon as I get there.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Tranquilo. Pero avísame cuando estés allí, ¿vale?
lines.meaning: No rush. But let me know when you're there, OK?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Claro. Y cuando tengas vacaciones, vienes a verme.
lines.meaning: Of course. And when you have a holiday, come and see me.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¡Hecho! Y no me voy de la playa hasta que me echen.
lines.meaning: Deal! And I'm not leaving the beach until they throw me out.

listening.text: Cuando llegues, llámame, por favor.
listening.meaning: When you arrive, call me, please.
listening.note: Arrival still to come: cuando + subjunctive.

listening.text: Siempre desayuno cuando me levanto.
listening.meaning: I always have breakfast when I get up.

listening.text: Antes de salir, cierra la ventana.
listening.meaning: Before going out, close the window.

listening.text: Antes de que empiece la película, compramos palomitas.
listening.meaning: Before the film starts, we'll buy popcorn.
listening.note: New word: las palomitas = the popcorn.

listening.text: Cuando llegué a la estación, mi amiga ya estaba allí.
listening.meaning: When I got to the station, my friend was already there.
listening.note: A past event keeps the indicative.

listening.text: Guarda el dinero en este sobre hasta que venga tu tía.
listening.meaning: Keep the money in this envelope until your aunt comes.
listening.note: New word: el sobre = the envelope.

listening.text: Mis padres trabajan mucho para que mi hermano y yo podamos estudiar.
listening.meaning: My parents work a lot so that my brother and I can study.

listening.text: En cuanto termine la reunión, te mando la factura por correo electrónico.
listening.meaning: As soon as the meeting ends, I'll send you the invoice by e-mail.
listening.note: New word: la factura = the invoice, the bill.

guide.tip: Ask one question: has it happened yet? If not, use the subjunctive. For a habit or the past, use the indicative. Never use the future after cuando.

bites.title: Not yet? Subjunctive
bites.rule: After cuando, a moment still to come takes the subjunctive. Habits and past events are facts, so they take the indicative. Never use cuando + future.
bites.example: Cuando llegues, te llamo. Cuando llego, me ducho.
bites.example_meaning: When you arrive, I'll call you. When I arrive, I have a shower.

bites.title: The same family
bites.rule: En cuanto (as soon as), hasta que (until) and después de que (after) follow the cuando rule: a future moment takes the subjunctive, a habit or the past takes the indicative.
bites.example_meaning: I'll wait for you until you come out.

bites.title: Antes de que: always
bites.rule: Antes de que takes the subjunctive every time, even for habits: at that moment the action hasn't happened.
bites.example: Siempre salgo antes de que llueva.
bites.example_meaning: I always go out before it rains.

bites.title: One subject takes the infinitive
bites.rule: Same subject in both halves? Drop que and use antes de, después de, hasta or para + infinitive. Para que + subjunctive is for someone else.
bites.example: Ahorro para viajar. Ahorro para que viajes.
bites.example_meaning: I save in order to travel. I save so that you can travel.

sorts.title: Subjunctive or indicative?
sorts.why: A moment still to come takes the subjunctive; what usually happens or already happened is a fact, so it takes the indicative.

items.text: En cuanto sepa algo, te aviso.
Siempre leo hasta que me duermo.

sorts.title: Infinitive or que + subjunctive?
sorts.why: One subject doing both things takes the infinitive. Two different people take que + subjunctive.

items.text: Habla despacio para que lo entiendan.

spots.why: A future moment after cuando takes the present subjunctive, never the future tense.

spots.sentence: Te aviso en cuanto sé algo.
spots.why: En cuanto + a moment still to come takes the subjunctive: sepa.

spots.sentence: Siempre me ducho cuando vuelva del gimnasio.
spots.why: Siempre marks a habit, so cuando takes the indicative.

spots.sentence: Salimos antes de que empieza a llover.
spots.why: Antes de que always takes the subjunctive.

spots.sentence: Te dejo mi coche para que llevas tus cosas.
spots.why: Para que always takes the subjunctive.

spots.sentence: Ayer, cuando llegue a casa, cené.
spots.why: Ayer = past, so the indicative preterite llegué (with accent), not the subjunctive llegue.

builds.meaning: When you have time, call me.
I'll wait for you until you come back.

builds.text: Lávate las manos antes de cenar.
Te lo explico para que lo entiendas.
builds.meaning: I'm explaining it so that you understand it.
As soon as I arrive, I'll let you know.

realm.content:
## Cuando… en Eldmark

Quest plans haven't happened yet, so they take the subjunctive: **cuando lleguemos a Highgate, venderemos el botín**; **en cuanto salga la luna, entramos en la mazmorra**; **la maga lanza un hechizo para que el orco no nos vea**. Tavern habits stay indicative: **cuando llueve, los enanos cantan**.

vocabulary.example: Cuando lleguemos a Highgate, venderemos el botín.
vocabulary.example_meaning: When we reach Highgate, we'll sell the loot.

vocabulary.example: En cuanto salga la luna, entramos en la mazmorra.
vocabulary.example_meaning: As soon as the moon rises, we go into the dungeon.

vocabulary.example: El paladín no va a descansar hasta que todos estén a salvo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The paladin isn't going to rest until everyone is safe.

vocabulary.example: Salid de la mazmorra antes de que se despierte el minotauro.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Get out of the dungeon before the minotaur wakes up.

vocabulary.example: La maga lanza un hechizo para que el orco no nos vea.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The mage casts a spell so that the orc doesn't see us.

vocabulary.example: Afila la espada antes de entrar en Deepanvil.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Sharpen your sword before going into Deepanvil.

vocabulary.example: Repartiremos el botín cuando volvamos a la taberna.
vocabulary.example_meaning: We'll share out the loot when we get back to the tavern.

vocabulary.example: No saldremos de la mazmorra hasta que encontremos la llave.
vocabulary.example_meaning: We won't leave the dungeon until we find the key.

vocabulary.example: En cuanto termine el hechizo, la puerta se abrirá.
vocabulary.example_meaning: As soon as the spell is finished, the door will open.

bites.title: Quest plans
bites.rule: A quest still to come: cuando, en cuanto, hasta que + subjunctive. Antes de que and para que always take it.
bites.example: Cuando volvamos a Frostmarch, compraremos una montura.
bites.example_meaning: When we get back to Frostmarch, we'll buy a mount.

listening.text: Cuando venga el orco, corremos.
listening.meaning: When the orc comes, we run.

listening.text: Esperad aquí hasta que vuelva la elfa.
listening.meaning: Wait here until the elf comes back.

listening.text: El enano come antes de entrar en la mina.
listening.meaning: The dwarf eats before going into the mine.

listening.text: Te doy esta poción para que te pongas bien.
listening.meaning: I'm giving you this potion so that you get better.
listening.note: New word: la poción = the potion.

listening.text: En cuanto amanezca, salimos hacia el Bosque Umbrío.
listening.meaning: As soon as day breaks, we set off for the Bosque Umbrío.

builds.meaning: When we reach Highgate, we'll rest.

builds.text: La maga nos ayuda para que ganemos.
builds.meaning: The mage helps us so that we win.

spots.sentence: Saldremos de la mazmorra cuando encontraremos la llave.
spots.why: Never the future tense after cuando: encontremos (subjunctive).

spots.sentence: El paladín reza antes de que empieza la batalla.
spots.why: Antes de que always takes the subjunctive.

sorts.title: Quest or habit?
sorts.why: Plans for the quest are not yet real, so they take the subjunctive. Habits and past battles are facts, so they take the indicative.

items.text: antes de que vuelva el orco

quiz.prompt: Venderemos el botín cuando ___ a Highgate.
quiz.explanation: The arrival is still to come, so cuando + present subjunctive: lleguemos. Cuando is never followed by the future.

quiz.prompt: La maga lanza un hechizo para que el orco no nos ___ (ver).
quiz.explanation: Different subjects (the mage, the orc), so para que + subjunctive: ver becomes vea.
hints: Para que always takes the subjunctive.

meadowbrook.content:
## Cuando… en la granja

Farm plans take the subjunctive: **cuando llegue la primavera, plantaré fresas**; **no voy a cosechar el maíz hasta que esté maduro**; **Rosa me guarda semillas para que pueda plantar calabazas**. What always happens on the farm stays indicative: **cuando llueve, las vacas se quedan en el granero**.

vocabulary.example: Cuando llegue la primavera, plantaré fresas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: When spring comes, I'll plant strawberries.

vocabulary.example: No voy a cosechar el maíz hasta que esté maduro.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'm not going to harvest the corn until it's ripe.

vocabulary.example: Después de que termine el festival, Leo volverá al río.
vocabulary.example_meaning: After the festival ends, Leo will go back to the river.

vocabulary.example: Rosa me guarda semillas para que pueda plantar calabazas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Rosa keeps seeds for me so that I can plant pumpkins.

vocabulary.example: Después de trabajar en la mina, Nora cena en la taberna.
vocabulary.example_meaning: After working in the mine, Nora has dinner at the tavern.

vocabulary.example: Ahorro dinero para comprar una vaca.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'm saving money to buy a cow.

vocabulary.example: En cuanto acabe la cosecha, haremos una fiesta.
vocabulary.example_meaning: As soon as the harvest is over, we'll have a party.

vocabulary.example: Cuando las calabazas estén maduras, las venderé en la tienda de Rosa.
vocabulary.example_meaning: When the pumpkins are ripe, I'll sell them at Rosa's shop.

vocabulary.example: Guarda el maíz en el granero antes de que llueva.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Put the corn in the barn before it rains.

bites.title: Planning the seasons
bites.rule: Plans for the next season take the subjunctive after cuando, en cuanto, hasta que and después de que. What always happens on the farm stays indicative.
bites.example: Cuando llegue el otoño, cosecharé las calabazas.
bites.example_meaning: When autumn comes, I'll harvest the pumpkins.

listening.text: Rosa abre la tienda antes de desayunar.
listening.meaning: Rosa opens the shop before having breakfast.

listening.text: Planto maíz para que coman las gallinas.
listening.meaning: I plant corn so that the hens can eat.

listening.text: Leo pesca hasta que se pone el sol.
listening.meaning: Leo fishes until the sun goes down.

listening.text: Cuando llegue el invierno, compraremos otra oveja.
listening.meaning: When winter comes, we'll buy another sheep.

listening.text: El alcalde hablará después de que termine el desfile.
listening.meaning: The mayor will speak after the parade ends.
listening.note: New word: el desfile = the parade.

builds.text: Cuando llegue el verano, iremos a la playa.
builds.meaning: When summer comes, we'll go to the beach.

builds.text: Te doy semillas para que plantes fresas.
builds.meaning: I'm giving you seeds so that you plant strawberries.

spots.sentence: Cosecharé las fresas cuando estarán maduras.
spots.why: Never the future tense after cuando: cuando estén maduras.

spots.sentence: Leo vuelve a casa antes de que se pone el sol.
spots.why: Antes de que always takes the subjunctive.

sorts.title: Which form after the time word?
sorts.why: Still to come takes the subjunctive. Habits and the past take the indicative. The same subject after a preposition takes the infinitive.

items.text: cuando nieva, me quedo en casa
hasta que la fresa esté madura

quiz.prompt: Cuando ___ (llegar) el invierno, guardaremos las vacas en el granero.
quiz.explanation: Winter is still to come, so cuando + present subjunctive: llegar becomes llegue (with -gu- to keep the hard g).
hints: Spelling: -gar verbs add a u before e to keep the hard g.

quiz.prompt: Compro semillas en la tienda de Rosa para ___ calabazas.
quiz.explanation: I buy the seeds and I plant the pumpkins: same subject, so para + infinitive. Para que + indicative is never correct.
hints: After para, the same subject takes the infinitive.

rustwake.content:
## Cuando… en el páramo

Out on the plains nobody knows what tomorrow brings, so plans take the subjunctive: **cuando pase la tormenta de ceniza, saldremos**; **en cuanto Leo repare la antena, escucharemos la radio**; **guarda agua filtrada para que tengas bastante**. What always happens stays indicative: **cuando hay polvo, cerramos la puerta**.

vocabulary.example: Cuando pase la tormenta de ceniza, saldremos a explorar.
vocabulary.example_meaning: When the ash storm passes, we'll go out exploring.

vocabulary.example: En cuanto Leo repare la antena, escucharemos la radio.
vocabulary.example_meaning: As soon as Leo repairs the aerial, we'll listen to the radio.

vocabulary.example: Volved a la cúpula antes de que se haga de noche.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Get back to the Dome before it gets dark.

vocabulary.example: Marta te guarda agua filtrada para que no tengas sed.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Marta is keeping filtered water for you so that you won't be thirsty.

vocabulary.example: No abras la puerta hasta que se vaya el escarabajo gigante.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Don't open the door until the giant beetle leaves.

vocabulary.example: Avísame por el radiorreloj cuando encuentres tuercas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Let me know over the wrist radio when you find nuts.

vocabulary.example: No salgas hasta que termine la tormenta de ceniza.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Don't go out until the ash storm is over.

vocabulary.example: Repararemos la antena antes de que llegue el capataz.
vocabulary.example_meaning: We'll repair the aerial before the foreman arrives.

vocabulary.example: Te llamo por el radiorreloj en cuanto llegue al mercado.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'll call you on the wrist radio as soon as I get to the market.

bites.title: Plans in the wasteland
bites.rule: On the plains every plan is not yet real: cuando, en cuanto, hasta que + subjunctive. Antes de que always takes it. Same subject? Use the infinitive.
bites.example: Antes de salir, carga el radiorreloj.
bites.example_meaning: Before going out, charge your wrist radio.

listening.text: Cuando hay polvo, cerramos la puerta.
listening.meaning: When it's dusty, we close the door.

listening.text: Te espero hasta que vuelvas del páramo.
listening.meaning: I'll wait for you until you come back from the plains.

listening.text: Cambio tuercas por agua para no tener sed.
listening.meaning: I trade nuts for water so as not to be thirsty.

listening.text: Llévate el tónico para que te pongas bien.
listening.meaning: Take the tonic so that you get better.
listening.note: New word: el tónico = the tonic.

listening.text: El capataz cierra la cúpula antes de que llueva.
listening.meaning: The foreman closes the Dome before it rains.
listening.note: New word: el capataz = the foreman.

builds.meaning: When the storm passes, we'll go out.

builds.text: Leo repara la radio para que la escuchemos.
builds.meaning: Leo is repairing the radio so that we can listen to it.

spots.sentence: Te llamo en cuanto llegaré al mercado.
spots.why: Never the future tense after en cuanto: en cuanto llegue.

spots.sentence: Marta guarda agua para que los buscadores no tienen sed.
spots.why: Para que always takes the subjunctive.

sorts.title: Plan or habit?
sorts.why: Plans still to come take the subjunctive (antes de que always does). Habits and the past are facts, so they take the indicative.

items.text: en cuanto Leo repare la antena
antes de que llegue el capataz

quiz.prompt: Saldremos a explorar en cuanto ___ la tormenta de ceniza.
quiz.explanation: The storm hasn't passed yet, so en cuanto + present subjunctive: pase. En cuanto is never followed by the future.

quiz.prompt: Avísame por el radiorreloj cuando ___ (encontrar, tú) agua filtrada.
quiz.explanation: Finding water is still to come, so cuando + subjunctive. Encontrar keeps its stem change: encuentro becomes encuentres.
hints: o changes to ue, and the -ar verb takes -es.

conversations.title: Before the storm
conversations.scenario: Leo el buscador wants to scavenge the ruined shopping centre; Marta la mercadera sells him supplies as an ash storm blows in.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Leo, ¿cuándo sales hacia el centro comercial en ruinas?
lines.meaning: Leo, when are you setting off for the ruined shopping centre?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: En cuanto pase la tormenta de ceniza. No quiero salir antes.
lines.meaning: As soon as the ash storm passes. I don't want to go out before then.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Bien pensado. Toma este tónico para que no te pongas enfermo.
lines.meaning: Good thinking. Take this tonic so that you don't get ill.

lines.speaker: b
lines.meaning: Thanks, Marta. How many nuts do I owe you?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Me pagas cuando vuelvas con algo bueno.
lines.meaning: You can pay me when you come back with something good.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Trato hecho. Te aviso por el radiorreloj antes de llegar.
lines.meaning: Deal. I'll let you know over the wrist radio before I arrive.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Y no vuelvas hasta que encuentres discos, ¿eh?
lines.meaning: And don't come back until you find some records, eh?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¡Ja! Cuando encuentre uno, lo escucharemos juntos.
lines.meaning: Ha! When I find one, we'll listen to it together.
